inShort: A tosses high balls, and B throws them down by hand first, then hits the same motion with the paddle as an overhead.
rules: An overhead is a hard shot hit from above your head, like a tennis serve. B stands near the baseline. A tosses slow, high, predictable balls to B.
First without paddles: B uses the empty hand and the natural throwing motion. Step, pull the elbow back, reach up, throw down.
The elbow and the feet move at the same time.
Then with the paddle in the throwing hand: A plays high balls, and B keeps the same order: elbow back, reach up, hit down.
Point your free hand at the ball. That gives you the distance and gets you to hit high and in front.
tooEasy: A mixes the depth and pace: one step for a near ball, two or more for a deep one. Even harder: A tosses a little to the left or right, so B has to move sideways before the overhead.
tooHard: Stay longer without the paddle, until the throwing motion and the footwork work together.
goodLooksLike: Contact high and in front, the free arm stays up, and the paddle finishes across to the opposite hip.
